claims_scope: variable-ranking behavior under mixed predictor cardinality; not clinical prediction or aetiology

dataset.cohort: NHANES August 2021 - August 2023 (cycle L), adults aged 20 and older with a glycohemoglobin measurement
dataset.source: CDC National Center for Health Statistics public-use SAS transport files
cohort_filters: complete cases on all 27 predictors after recoding each variable's documented refused/don't-know codes to missing
dataset.filter_leakage_note: cohort filters and missing-code recoding never read the outcome and are applied once outside cross-validation; the three shuffled control columns are permuted once from the base seed and then treated as fixed data columns
dataset.cohort_note: an earlier design-verification probe reported n = 2975 because it recoded 7 and 9 as missing in every questionnaire column, which are valid answers for alcohol frequency and sedentary minutes; the per-variable codes here are taken from the cycle L codebooks and were fixed before any fold was run

outcome.name: diabetes
outcome.definition: LBXGH >= 6.5 percent OR DIQ010 == 1 (told by a doctor you have diabetes)
outcome.exclusion_note: these define or restate the outcome; including any of them would be circular

encoding_note: all predictors are numeric NHANES codes or measurements and are passed identically to every method; no method receives factor typing, so the comparison is on matched input
mec_weight_note: WTMEC2YR is the examination sampling weight, a survey-design quantity with close to one distinct value per participant; it is retained as a natural high-cardinality predictor whose association with the outcome is not of clinical interest

shuffled_controls.construction: each is an independent permutation of the source column drawn once from numpy default_rng(base_seed), so it is noise by construction with the source's marginal distribution and cardinality

methods.rf: scikit-learn RandomForestClassifier at shipped defaults, n_estimators = profile trees; importance = impurity decrease (feature_importances_)
methods.cif: citrees ConditionalInferenceForestClassifier, selector mc, threshold_method histogram, max_thresholds 32, n_estimators = profile trees, other parameters shipped defaults; importance = feature_importances_
methods.cforest: partykit::cforest via paper.benchmark.pipeline.r_methods.r_cforest_importance at partykit shipped defaults (teststat quadratic, testtype Univariate, mincriterion 0, mtry ceiling(sqrt(p)), replace FALSE, fraction 0.632), ntree = profile trees; importance = varimp(conditional = FALSE)
methods.ranking: features ranked 1 (largest importance) to p+3 within each training fold; tied importances, which are common when a conditional-inference forest never selects a feature, receive their midrank so that unselected features are not ordered arbitrarily

outer_folds.note: importances and ranks are computed on the training fold; held-out data are used only for the descriptive prediction metrics

primary_test.estimand: mean over folds of rank(shuffled_mec_weight | rf) - rank(shuffled_mec_weight | cif)
primary_test.alternative_note: a lower rank number means the method treats the noise column as more important; the hypothesis is that RF ranks the high-cardinality noise column as more important than citrees does

cardinality_correlation.estimand: mean over folds of spearman(importance_rf, n_unique_train) - spearman(importance_cif, n_unique_train)
cardinality_correlation.note: n_unique is computed on the training fold for all 30 columns

low_cardinality_clinical_block.estimand: mean over folds of mean_rank(block | rf) - mean_rank(block | cif)
low_cardinality_clinical_block.note: the eight predictors with at most three levels, excluding the shuffled controls; the hypothesis is that RF ranks this block as less important than citrees does

descriptive.reference_agreement: per-fold spearman between cif and cforest ranks, and between rf and cforest ranks, reported with fold means and 95 percent bootstrap intervals over repeats; no hypothesis test
descriptive.shuffled_sex_negative_control: rank of shuffled_sex under every method; expected near the bottom for all methods, showing the contrast is about cardinality and not about shuffling
descriptive.shuffled_age_control: rank of shuffled_age under every method, the medium-cardinality point between the two

prediction.model: logistic_regression_l2_C1 on the top-k features of each method, fit on the training fold, scored on the held-out fold
prediction.note: reported to show that the ranking differences do not come from one method being a weaker predictor; no hypothesis test

descriptive.runtime: wall-clock seconds per method per fold, reported as medians

positive_control.rule: waist or total_chol or triglycerides or hdl must be in the top 5 of every method in a majority of folds; and shuffled_sex must be outside the top 20 for every method in a majority of folds
positive_control.note: the first checks the pipeline recovers known metabolic correlates; the second checks the shuffled controls really are noise

missing_codes_note: NHANES refused / don't-know codes, per variable as documented in the cycle L codebooks; other predictors are measurements with no reserved codes
